transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because... I've been really struggling to get by ever since a terrible thing happened to me about a year and nine months ago. I just haven't been able to move past it at all, and it feels like it's taking over my life. I... I really don't know what to do anymore.
I'm so sorry you've been carrying this for so long. Do you find yourself experiencing upsetting, unwanted memories, nightmares, or moments where you feel like you are reliving that event?

Yes, I do. During the day, sudden and unwanted memories of the event just pop into my head, and sometimes it feels so real that I feel like I'm actually reliving it all over again. I also suffer from terrible nightmares about it almost every night, and I wake up completely distressed.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid thoughts, feelings, places, or conversations that remind you of that event?

Yes, absolutely. I do everything I can to block out any thoughts or feelings about it, and I completely avoid certain places, people, or conversations because they bring back too much pain. Honestly, it is incredibly exhausting to constantly keep my guard up just to stay away from those reminders.
Have you also been feeling constantly on edge, irritable, or unusually jumpy and easily startled since the event?

Yes, I've been extremely irritable and constantly on edge. My nerves feel so sharp and sensitive that I find myself snapping at people easily. I live in a constant state of tension and fear, as if I'm always waiting for some kind of danger.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder, and Major Depressive Disorder. The patient has now confirmed experiencing intrusive memories, flashbacks, nightmares, active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, and persistent hyperarousal (irritability, tension, being on edge) lasting for 21 months since a traumatic event. These symptoms meet the full criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, making it the definitive diagnosis, while Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Major Depressive Disorder are ruled out as the primary diagnosis.
